## ✨ Highlights

- 🏗️ **Clusters as code**: Terraform's `janus_cluster` makes a cluster of new machines on the Controller's hypervisors - each on a physical host of its own by default -, its member count, auto-scaling and balancer hook changed in place, its machines destroyed with it ([Terraform](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/terraform.md#janus_cluster)).
- 🔀 **A balancer in front, told which members serve**: a cloud load balancer, a router's ECMP routes or another HAProxy in front of a cluster is told before a member stops serving - the operation waiting for its answer - and once one serves ([a balancer in front](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/clusters.md#a-balancer-in-front)).
- ⚖️ **A cluster's machines go where there is the most memory**: made, recycled or added by scaling, a new machine goes to the host with the most memory to give, never to one without room for it ([on new machines](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/clusters.md#on-new-machines)).
- 📈 **The Controller's own Prometheus endpoint**: each cluster's members and load, the figures auto-scaling judges ([the Controller's metrics](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/metrics.md#the-controllers-metrics)).
- 🔁 **A new node pulls the old node's state itself**: `janusctl -n new system state import -from old` - the state goes from node to node, never through your machine nor the Controller ([node to node](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/replacing-a-node.md#node-to-node)).

## 🔄 Since the v2026.10.25 pre-release

- 🔀 **The balancer hook** (below, [#308](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/308)), 📈 **the Controller's metrics** ([#302](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/302)) and 🔁 **node-to-node state transfer** ([#304](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/304)) - new.
- What [its lab campaign](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/main/docs/pre-release-tests/v2026.10.25.md) found ([#309](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/309)):
  - 🐛 With anti-affinity preferred, recycling a member alone on its host put the new machine beside another member, the cluster then on one host: the replaced member's host is now kept when the others would mean sharing one ([#303](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/303)).
  - 🐛 A scale the hosts can't give answered 202, then failed in the cluster's error: it is refused at once (400), saying why, nothing made ([#303](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/303)).
  - A recycle journaled the old member's drain twice; a memory refusal gave each host's memory after the request's earlier machines without saying so; the policy's bounds came in Go's format ("1m0s to 1h0m0s") - all fixed ([#303](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/303)).
- 📖 Why a VM's firmware reboot takes 30-40 s longer now and then - its UEFI firmware compacting its variable store, about once every 40 boots - and how to avoid it ([#307](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/307)).

## 🔗 Clusters

- **`janus_cluster` in the Terraform provider** ([#299](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/299)):
  - `name`, the `hypervisors` its machines may go to, `anti_affinity` (`required` by default, `preferred`, `off`), `members`, the `machine` each member is (size, release, extensions, HAProxy branch, kernel, image, DHCP interfaces, DNS, NTP) and `autoscaling` (`observe`, `on`, `off`, its bounds and thresholds).
  - **`members` changes in place**: a member more is a new machine like the newest, placed by the anti-affinity; a member less is the newest, drained, taken out and destroyed. With `autoscaling` `on` it is the count the cluster starts with - the Controller decides afterwards, `current_members` says what it has.
  - **`autoscaling` changes in place**; removed, auto-scaling is off. So does **`balancer`** - the hook below; its `secret` sensitive, never read back.
  - `name`, `hypervisors`, `anti_affinity` and `machine` make a new cluster; moving one to a newer release member by member is a recycle on the Controller.
  - Destroying it ends the cluster, then destroys its machines - those auto-scaling made too.
  - Computed: `current_members`, `member_names`, `machine_ids`. No import: the machine specification isn't read back from the Controller.
- **A balancer in front** ([#308](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/308), [a balancer in front](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/clusters.md#a-balancer-in-front)): a cluster's hook, a POST of every member - its name, address, template variables, in service or not - so the receiver makes its targets the members in service, and a call it missed is made good by the next.
  - `in` once a member serves: it joined, was undrained, took a recycled member's place.
  - `out` **before** a member stops serving - drained, removed, replaced, a step in: the operation waits for the hook's answer, then the drain delay, and a hook that doesn't answer stops it, the member serving on (a removal with *force* goes on).
  - `sync` when the hook is saved, after a removal, and from the 10-minute check whenever the list changed or a call failed.
  - Signed with HMAC-SHA256 of the body (`X-Janus-Signature-256`) when a secret is set - kept sealed, write-only; HTTPS against the system's CAs or the one you give.
  - The cluster's **Members** tab, **Balancer in front**; `PUT /api/clusters/{id}/balancer`; `janusctl cluster balancer NAME -url ...`; Terraform's `balancer` block. The **Drain** button now tells the balancer first.
- **The Controller's metrics** ([#302](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/302)): `GET /api/metrics` on the Controller's main port, for a reader or an API token (Prometheus `authorization` Bearer) - `janus_cluster_members`, `janus_cluster_load_*` (HAProxy idle, CPUs busy and steal, connections over maxconn, 0 to 1), `janus_cluster_autoscale_*`. The members' load is now read for every cluster, auto-scaled or not, and `GET /api/clusters/{id}` gives it as `load`.
- **A scale the cluster can't have is refused at once** (400), saying why: hosts, memory, the policy's ceilings, members that aren't the Controller's machines ([#303](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/303)).
- **Placement by memory** ([#300](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/300)): among the hosts the anti-affinity allows, the one with the most memory free goes first - what a host keeps free (a twentieth, 512 MiB at least) aside, and what the same request already put there counted -; the order of the hypervisors given only breaks ties.
  - A host without room for one more machine is never picked: with too little memory anywhere, the cluster is refused before anything is made, saying what each host has.
  - With anti-affinity `off`, machines no longer go round the hypervisors in turn: they go where the memory is.
  - A recycle tries the hosts other than the replaced member's first - its memory is freed only once it leaves -, unless they would mean sharing a host: then the replaced member's own, the new machine alone there once the member leaves; a member more is placed the same way.
- **The auto-scaling policy's durations are in seconds** in the API: `out_after_seconds`, `in_after_seconds`, `out_cooldown_seconds`, `in_cooldown_seconds` - like a machine's policy - where v2026.10.24-6 gave nanoseconds ([#299](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/299)).
- The cluster's journal names a new machine's hypervisor ("on kvm02") where it gave the record's id ([#297](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/297)).

## 🔁 Replacing a node

- **Node to node** ([#304](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/304), [node to node](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/replacing-a-node.md#node-to-node)): `janusctl -n new system state import -from old` (`-identity`, `-save-network` as before). The new node makes a key for it; the old node signs its request with its own CA - a certificate good for ten minutes and **one** export, the identity only if granted; the new node pulls the state with it and restarts into it. No key leaves the node that made it, the state never touches your machine, and the Controller is never on the way. `-from HOST:PORT` with the old node's credentials for a node outside your context; `-from-address` when the new node reaches the old one elsewhere.
- API: `SystemService.StateExportGrant` (on the old node) and `StateImportFrom` (on the new one), admins only, refused through the Controller.

## 🧪 Tests

- `terraform-provider-test`: a `janus_cluster` of two new machines on the libvirt container, scaled to three and back to two in place - the third's machine destroyed -, its auto-scaling set, a plan with nothing left after each step, and destroyed with its machines.
- `terraform-provider-test` also sets the cluster's balancer hook - a receiver checking each call's signature - and checks it is told of the third member coming in, and of it going before it is drained.
- `qemu-controller-cluster-test`: a drain told to the balancer first, signed, the undrain after, a removal told before and the list without it after.
- `qemu-state-migrate-test`: a third node pulling the first one's state itself, through an address its certificate doesn't name; the refusals (a reader's grant, another node's credentials, a node in use).
- `controller-libvirt-test` checks the journal names the hypervisor on a recycle and a scale-out; the placement's unit tests cover memory in every anti-affinity mode, and a preferred recycle keeping hosts apart.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Auto-scaling policy fields**: `GET /api/clusters/{id}` and `PUT /api/clusters/{id}/autoscale` now use `*_seconds`. The nanosecond fields v2026.10.24-5 and -6 used (`out_after`, `in_after`, `out_cooldown`, `in_cooldown`) are still read - a policy saved by v2026.10.24-6 keeps its values -, but a script reading them should move to the new names.
- **`janus_cluster` needs a Controller on this version**: an older one doesn't read the policy in seconds, nor has the balancer hook.
- **A cluster's Drain button with a balancer hook** waits for the hook: one that doesn't answer refuses the drain, the member serving on.
- **Node-to-node state transfer** needs both nodes on this version.
- **Where machines go**: a cluster on hypervisors whose order you relied on - the first hypervisor first - is now placed by memory; the order only breaks ties.
